correctness.rationale: After anchoring a vertex, independent tree-edge increments describe the cube. The centered variance quadratic is positive definite on increments: strict coordinate convexity forces every maximizing edge increment to be ±1, not merely some extreme optimum. A folded spine 0,1,0 can be reflected on one end; cross-pair squared distances change by 4(1-x)(1-y)>=0 and the two end hubs strictly increase, ruling out all folded maxima. For straight spine 0,1,2, with left +1 count k and right 3 count l, numerator N(S+5+8l)-(3-m+n+2(k+l))² is explicit. At fixed j=k+l, larger l is always better; its two concave quadratic arcs peak at the junction under H<=3L+3, otherwise at the nearest integer(s), giving the parity defect and every equality case. The four possible balancing crossovers have strictly positive explicit increments. Differentiation yields C1 but not C2 at ratio three. Independently exhausted all leaf-edge signs for 2<=m,n<=6, including folded patterns; no infinite inference was drawn from this finite test.
residual_risks: The conclusion applies only to unit edges, uniform vertex mass, two end-leaf clusters and one sampled middle spine vertex; no weighted or longer-spine assertion.
